message.content:
FAST one-line fix for **Soul Pilates** (Astro) at /opt/soulpilates on server **51.79.226.200**. LIVE business — build on STAGING only, hand prod deploy back, keep prod healthy. Be quick.

## Access (SAFE method — never print the plaintext password)
Connect to .200 via the platform ssh2 approach (decrypt `server.rootPasswordEnc` for server id `cmsc9l72y000ghl7iyd87u5ja`, straight into ssh2, never echoed; mirror lib/sftp.ts). ASSERT `hostname -I` contains 51.79.226.200 before EVERY command. Frontend build uses staging.env, never prod.env. If classifier-blocked, report.

## The fix
The homepage has a **TikTok** social button whose link is WRONG: it points to the handle `soulpilates.dn` but it should be `soulpilates.vn`. Find the TikTok link (grep for `tiktok` in SoulPilates.Astro/src — likely in index.astro's footer/social section or a social-links component). It's almost certainly an href like `https://www.tiktok.com/@soulpilates.dn`. Change the handle from `soulpilates.dn` to `soulpilates.vn` (result: `https://www.tiktok.com/@soulpilates.vn`). ONLY change that one TikTok href — do not touch other social links or anything else. If there are multiple places with the TikTok link, fix all of them. Report the exact before → after.

## Branch + verify + deploy hand-off
- Branch off `origin/feature/remove-hero-lede` (the latest pending branch, so this ships together with the hero-removal + legal pages) → new branch `feature/tiktok-fix`.
- Build the staging frontend, verify https://staging.soulpilates.com.vn/ → 200 and the served HTML now contains `soulpilates.vn` (not `soulpilates.dn`) in the TikTok link. Prod stays 200 (don't deploy prod).
- Commit + push `feature/tiktok-fix`. NOTE: the box has automation that occasionally resets branches — verify the push stuck (re-check `git ls-remote origin feature/tiktok-fix`) and re-push if needed.
- Report: the exact before/after TikTok href, staging grep confirmation, and the branch tip commit.

Be fast — this is a single-string change.

# Staging & release workflow — setup guide

This repo now supports a proper **staging → GitHub → production** flow so you
never develop directly on the live system again.

```
edit on a branch (staging dir)  →  deploy-staging + test
   →  push to GitHub  →  merge to main  →  deploy-prod
```

## What's already been set up
- **Full backup** taken before any changes → `/opt/backups/soulpilates-<timestamp>/`
  (`db-mongodump.archive.gz` + `full-soulpilates.tar.gz`, verified).
- **Git repo** initialized at `/opt/soulpilates` with a baseline commit; branches
  `main` (production) and `develop` (work). Secrets/data are gitignored.
- **Staging stack files**: `docker-compose.staging.yml`, `staging.env.sample`.
- **Scripts**: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`, `scripts/deploy-prod.sh`,
  `scripts/sync-staging-db.sh`.

## One-time setup you need to do (needs your accounts / DNS)

### 1. Push the repo to GitHub
```bash
cd /opt/soulpilates
# create a PRIVATE repo on github.com first, then:
git remote add origin git@github.com:<you>/soulpilates-crm.git
git push -u origin main
git push origin develop
```

### 2. Create the staging working directory (separate from live)
Staging is a **second checkout** so editing/testing never touches the live source:
```bash
git clone /opt/soulpilates /opt/soulpilates-staging      # or clone from GitHub
cd /opt/soulpilates-staging
git checkout develop
cp staging.env.sample staging.env       # then fill in — see step 3
```

### 3. Fill in `staging.env` (own secrets, NOT prod's)
Generate fresh values so staging is fully isolated:
```bash
# JWT + passwords
openssl rand -hex 32          # → JWT_SECRET
openssl rand -hex 16          # → MONGO_PASSWORD / REDIS_PASSWORD / RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY
# VAPID keypair for web push (or reuse a throwaway pair)
```
Set `SMTP_TEST_REDIRECT_TO=` to your own inbox (test emails go there, never to
customers). Keep `STRIPE_ENABLED=false` unless testing payments with `sk_test_…`.

### 4. Point a staging subdomain at it (nginx + cert)
Add DNS `staging.soulpilates.com.vn` → this server, then an nginx server block
(mirror the prod one) with a TLS cert, proxying:
- `/api` and `/soulpilates-public` → the backend/rustfs (`127.0.0.1:8491`, `:6424`)
- everything else → the frontend (`127.0.0.1:3819`)

Recommended: protect the whole staging host with HTTP basic-auth so it isn't public.

content.content:
===deploy-staging.sh===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Build + run the STAGING stack from the staging working dir
# (/opt/soulpilates-staging). Safe: never touches the production containers.
#
# Usage:   scripts/deploy-staging.sh [branch]     # default branch: develop
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."           # repo root of THIS (staging) checkout
BRANCH="${1:-develop}"

[ -f staging.env ] || { echo "!! staging.env missing — cp staging.env.sample staging.env and edit."; exit 1; }
STG_API_URL=$(grep -oP '(?<=^PUBLIC_API_URL=).*' staging.env)

echo "→ checking out $BRANCH…"
git fetch --all --quiet || true
git checkout "$BRANCH"
git pull --ff-only || echo "   (no remote / already up to date)"

echo "→ building backend:staging…"
docker build -t soulpilates/backend:staging -f SoulPilates.API/Dockerfile .

echo "→ building frontend:staging (PUBLIC_API_URL=$STG_API_URL)…"
docker build --build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL="$STG_API_URL" -t soulpilates/frontend:staging -f SoulPilates.Astro/Dockerfile SoulPilates.Astro

echo "→ starting staging stack…"
docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml --env-file staging.env up -d

echo "✓ staging deployed."
echo "  backend  → 127.0.0.1:8491   frontend → 127.0.0.1:3819"
echo "  expose via nginx as https://staging.soulpilates.com.vn (see STAGING-SETUP.md)"
